title: Improve Dedicated Fleet Autoscaler: burst controls + utilization reporting (v11)
author: Ava Chen
description: Context: Dedicated fleets sometimes exhaust burst capacity or produce misleading utilization metrics during short-lived traffic spikes. This PR is the v11 iteration of the autoscaler and reporting work: it decouples burst bookkeeping from long-term utilization, adds quota-aware burst admission controls, and exposes more actionable utilization windows in the observability stack. Motivation: reduce unexpected throttles, improve SLA guarantees for committed capacity, and give SRE and customers clearer signals for tuning reserved capacity. This description is a single continuous string that includes the motivation, what changed, and rollout/rollback notes. What changed: 1) Autoscaler: split 'burst' accounting into a separate admission path and implemented a token-bucket style burst pool per-fleet with configurable refill rates and max-burst tokens. 2) Throughput guarantees: added per-fleet min-throughput enforcement for reserved capacity; when enforced, requests are prioritized and throttles are applied to non-reserved traffic paths. 3) Utilization reporting: new telemetry (fleet.burst_tokens, fleet.burst_admissions, fleet.min_throughput_enforced, utilization_window_{1m,5m,1h}) exported to Prometheus and forwarded to metrics pipeline; added Grafana dashboard panels and alerts for burst saturation and sustained under-utilization. 4) Helm and installer: new values in redwood-helm-charts for burstPolicy, minThroughput, and utilizationReporting toggles. 5) Tests & benchmarks: unit tests for burst admission logic, integration tests simulating mixed reserved/non-reserved traffic, and a small perf canary validating tail latency under burst. Rollout: feature-gated behind config flag 'fleet.autoscaler.v11.enabled' and staged rollout to canary fleets; default off for existing customers. Migration: when toggled on, existing fleet metadata is backfilled with a conservative burst token allocation; operators can run the provided migration script to tune refill rates. Rollback: revert the feature flag and deploy a migration that drains burst pools gracefully. Related: references ENG-3125 (earlier autoscaler refactor) and SRE-1982 (incident analysis that motivated burst limits).
commits: decouple autoscaler burst accounting (core/autoscaler: separate burst pool) - move burst logic into burst_pool.go - introduce TokenBucket struct and unit tests
add metrics exporter for fleet burst and utilization (observability/metrics) - export fleet.burst_tokens, fleet.burst_admissions, fleet.min_throughput_enforced - add labels: fleet_id, region, tier
helm: add burstPolicy/minThroughput config and values.yaml entries
integration tests: simulate reserved vs best-effort traffic and verify enforcement and metrics
docs: add runbook and dashboard screenshots for new panels
perf: small canary harness to measure tail latency under configured burst scenarios
review_comments: Diego Martinez: Nice separation of concerns. Two asks: (1) please add a brief note in autoscaler README about the expected token refill units (tokens/sec) and how they relate to request units, (2) I think minThroughput enforcement should expose the current enforced_tps metric (so operators can track when min throughput is being actively used).
Ava Chen (author): Thanks Diego - added README note and exposed fleet.min_throughput_enforced as a gauge in metrics_exporter; updated tests to assert metric emission.

Priya Nandakumar: Integration test looks good but saw a flaky assertion in the canary harness under high variance. Can we add a retry/assert-within-window instead of strict equality? Also please bump the observability retention for the new metrics to 30d in the docs.
Ava Chen: Updated canary to assert within 95th percentile window and adjusted doc to recommend 30d retention. Added an e2e test that reproduces the earlier flaky behavior to prevent regressions.

Liam O'Connor: Approving pending one small nit: make the default refill rate more conservative (0.1 tokens/sec) for existing fleets to avoid sudden token bursts on flip. Also recommend a post-deploy runbook step to verify steady-state. Marked approval after that change.
Ava Chen: Adjusted default refill rate, added runbook step, and squashed commits per maintainers guidance.
ci_checks: integration-tests: pass (simulated reserved vs best-effort flows)
merge_summary: Merged via squash by Priya Nandakumar on 2026-02-20. Commit message: "feat(autoscaler): burst token pool + min throughput enforcement + utilization telemetry (v11)". Release note entry added; feature gated by fleet.autoscaler.v11.enabled; rollout started to canary fleets 2026-02-21.
release_notes:
- Introduces token-bucket burst pool per fleet (configurable refill and max tokens)
- Adds per-fleet min throughput enforcement for reserved capacity
- Exposes new telemetry: fleet.burst_tokens, fleet.burst_admissions, fleet.min_throughput_enforced, utilization_window_1m/5m/1h
- Helm values: burstPolicy, minThroughput, utilizationReporting
- Backfill migration script included for conservative default allocations
- Feature gated; disabled by default for existing customers
